stem: At a patient's request, a DEA-registered pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription once to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. What pathway applies?

choices.text: Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
Use the one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer pathway if Massachusetts law and all federal conditions are satisfied.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.

explanation.core_reasoning: At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists. morphine (MS Contin) is used for severe and persistent pain requiring extended opioid treatment. It is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.
